extracted.intended_audience: suppliers/contractors and government procurement officers involved in Indian Service contracts (1880-era bids and awards)
extracted.subtask_description: Record of proposals received and contracts awarded (advertisement May 10, 1880) for hardware and medical supplies for the Indian Service; documents bid items, quantities, unit measures, delivery points, prices, footnotes, and the basis for awards. Useful for interpreting historical procurement requirements and award criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding on comparison of samples
rubrics_metrics.description: "awards were made on comparison of samples with which each bid was accompanied."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts were awarded based on comparison of physical samples submitted with bids; sample quality determined acceptability (examples: note about King's quality 'not perfect'; alternate bids for steel-pointed picks recorded). This implies that bidders must submit representative samples and that evaluation prioritizes actual sample quality over price alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures in large type denote awarded rates
rubrics_metrics.description: "Figures in large type denote the rates at which contracts have been awarded"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published table highlights, via typographic convention (large type), which bid rates resulted in awards. Readers should identify awarded prices by this typographic cue when interpreting the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of delivery specified and binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Each line item includes a 'Points of delivery' column listing delivery locations (e.g., Chicago, Kansas City, New York, Philadelphia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery location is a required element of the bid and affects pricing and award; footnotes sometimes indicate 'Delivered in New York' or 'Delivered in Kansas City.' Bidders must meet the specified delivery point(s) for the quantities and price quoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed item specification required (size/material/form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Line-item descriptions specify item form, size, and material (e.g., 'Iron, flat-bar, 1 by 1 inch', 'Knives, hunting, 6-inch, ebony handle, with bolster').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids must match the precise specification (dimensions, material, finish, handles, type) in the advertisement. The report shows that acceptance depends on conformity to these detailed specs; footnotes further refine required features (see 'with ears, gauge, and handles', 'platform, 21 by 30', etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of measure and pricing units standardized
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantities and prices are given in standard units (pounds, dozen, gross, per 1,000, sets, dozens, pieces) with prices shown as dollars/cents per unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must quote in the specified unit (e.g., per pound, per dozen, per gross). The award record uses these units to compare and record awarded rates, so inaccurate unit quoting can cause miscomparison or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer/source identification noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Some bids include manufacturer/source statements (e.g., 'All iron on this bid manufactured by L. Oliver & Phillips, Pittsburgh.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of manufacturer or source may be required or recorded and can affect award decisions (brand/producer quality). Bidders may declare manufacture origin and quality assurance in their bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity limits or availability constraints declared
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain entries specify limited availability (e.g., '8 dozen only', '2 dozen only', 'f to 1 inch only').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders may limit quantities they can supply; such limitations are recorded and considered in award decisions. Contracting officers and bidders must pay attention to availability notes when matching awarded quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes and special-condition annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous footnotes (marked a, b, c, d, e, etc.) qualify items, e.g., 'a All iron on this bid manufactured by L. Oliver & Phillips, Pittsburgh.'; 'b Complete, with timbers, and frame ready to set up.'; 'd Platform, 21 by 30.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes contain binding exceptions, packaging, component, or installation requirements and pricing conditions. Bidders must comply with these special conditions; evaluators use them to interpret bid conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discounts and conditional price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: 'd Discount of 10 per cent, to be made on locks.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some bids include price discounts or conditional adjustments that affect the effective award price. Such conditional pricing is explicitly recorded and applied as noted (e.g., percentage discounts on specified items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging and presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Items specify packaging or presentation (e.g., 'Putty, in bladders', 'Cerate ... in 1-pound tins', 'Castor oil, in 32-oz. bottles', 'Shovels ... "sacked"').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packaging form is a contractual requirement; bids are compared on correctly packaged goods. Improper packaging or incorrect container sizes could render a bid nonconforming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation of quality exceptions or imperfect lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific quality notes appear in the report (e.g., 'King's quality, 4 and 5 pounds, not perfect.'; 'Bid also received from H. Wells for steel-pointed earth picks at $5 per dozen. King's quality ... not perfect.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation recorded and reports quality defects found in samples or lots; quality defects influence awards and may lead to rejection despite price. Bidders must ensure sample quality matches specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing format and currency/cents precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Prices are shown with dollar and cent precision, sometimes in cents-only columns (e.g., 'Cents. 10.98'), and with typographic marks indicating fractions or footnote ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must quote prices with the precision and format required; the published awards record uses cents and fractional notations to capture exact awarded rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to advertisement/date of call for bids
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Abstract of proposals received and contracts awarded in New York City, under advertisement of May 10, 1880, for goods for the Indian service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids are responses to a specific advertisement/call for proposals; eligibility and terms are anchored to that solicitation date and specifications. Bidders must respond to the stated advertisement and its requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item-specific accessory/inclusion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some item lines require accessories or completions (examples: 'Spirit-levels, 26 inches, with plumb', 'Saws ... With ears, gauge, and handles', 'Vise, gunsmiths', ... 'parallel, filers, 4-inch jaw').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids must include specified accessories or complete assemblies as part of the item; omissions can cause nonconformance. The award record notes these inclusions to ensure comparability among bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record of proposals and awarded contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The document publishes the proposals received, quantities, unit prices, delivery points, footnotes, and awarded rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement outcomes and the basis for awards (sample comparison, awarded rates) are documented publicly for transparency. Contractors should expect public reporting of awards and the criteria used.
